complexity_ledger.narrative: specs/results/scorecards/score-drives-validation/GOAL-scored-at-goal-time/SV-03/RESULT.md is the evidence ledger, ESCALATION.md beside it is the proposal, and `references/goal_score_wiring.md` (SV-06) is the design this implements. WHAT WAS BUILT. The four diffs SV-06 handed off, cut against the INSTALLED skill files, verified to apply cleanly and independently in either order, and ESCALATED rather than applied -- skills are READ from this repository and never edited from it, and `skill-manager sync` was not run. The installed files are re-hashed before and after every demonstration run and reported UNCHANGED. WHAT WAS MEASURED, at tree 5620c9a over 109 plans on disk. SV-06's 0-of-27 is a string test; this ticket resolved every `baseline.evidence` against the filesystem and asked the question the evaluation ticket actually has to answer -- can you OPEN the card that produced the number? Of 27 distinct goals, 18 name a judged instrument and 0 OF THOSE 18 have a baseline that can be opened: 8 cite a directory, 8 cite a document, 1 cites a path that does not resolve at all, and 1 is pure prose. 87 sealed cards sit uncited. The judged denominator is 18, not 27 (SV-03-DF-02, `denominator_rule`) -- the correction makes the compliance rate worse. R1, ON A REAL EPIC PLAN. `GOAL-loop-reaches-the-program` in this epic's own live plan cites `specs/results/scorecards/close-the-loop/`, which contains ZERO scorecard.json files -- the CL-03 cards are in two sibling directories. The evaluation ticket is not asked to pick a card out of a folder; it is handed a folder with no card in it. Sealed at eab2883, never edited, pinned by a test whose docstring says to MOVE the demonstration rather than delete it if the plan is ever repaired. A SECOND FAILING INPUT, AIMED AT THE PROPOSAL ITSELF. SV-06's verbatim wording for edit 2 asks for "the path to the SINGLE sealed card". Two judged goals here have baselines that are figures over a POPULATION of cards -- including `GOAL-D2-can-move`, the goal SV-06 holds up as the best of its kind -- so the sentence is unsatisfiable for them. The shipped wording asks for enumerability, not singularity. Filed as SV-03-DF-01 rather than editing a predecessor's sealed page. ABSENCE, DESIGNED FOR AND DEMONSTRATED. A complete epic plan with no card anywhere validates identically through a pristine copy of the three skill units and through a copy with all four diffs applied -- same exit code, same stdout. 331 words are added across the four diffs and 0 of them bind a project with no card, because every added block opens with a conditional such a project fails. The guard check is shown FAILING on an unguarded sentence so it cannot pass vacuously. NO NEW GATE, and the temptation was real: the classifier is written and `return 1` is one line. It has no failing exit path at all, nothing in `scripts/` reads it, and two tests assert both. The thing a checker would gate is the epic owner's prose about their own baseline. COST. `serve | wc -c` is 6,281 bytes at 9 rungs and digest sha256:2d7d4a0506d9b259 before and after -- unchanged, because nothing here touches `references/eval_scorecard.md`. The card does not learn about the goal process; the goal process learns to name a card. FIVE FINDINGS FILED, NONE FIXED: SV-03-DF-01 through DF-05.

refinement.detail: Searched, found none, and the search had a real subject rather than a formality. SV-03's `model_delta_expectation` is `none expected`, `desired_actions` is empty, and `diff -rq specs/tickets/SV-03/current specs/tickets/SV-03/desired` is EMPTY -- the TLA+ model, the configs, the adapters and the spec-unit tests are byte-identical to the project `current` they were seeded from, so there is no representation this ticket added and none it can refine away. The refinement question that DID have a subject is the one outside the model: whether the wiring needed a `dimension:` field, a `scored_by:` block, a `score_signal:` field, a `--goal` flag on `score_tools.py`, or a checker. Every one was considered and every one was refused -- SV-06 built and validated two of them at exit 0 and rejected them anyway, and SV-03 re-checked rather than inherited that. The ticket ships FOUR PROSE EDITS to files it does not own, zero new fields, zero new gates and zero bytes to `serve`. The cheapest carrier that does the job is the standing rule and this is it.

ticket.objective: Scoped by SV-06's design and SV-02's answer. Today scoring happens in an evaluation ticket as a separate act and NO GOAL HAS EVER BEEN KEYED TO A DIMENSION. Build: a goal can declare a scored dimension and a subject, so 'this epic improves modularity' is a claim the card SETTLES rather than prose the evaluation re-derives; A BASELINE IS SCORED AT DECLARATION AND SEALED, because this project's whole record shows baselines written from memory and later found wrong; it must work for a project that is NOT THIS ONE, with no path, fixture or dimension id that only exists here; and IT MUST BE OPTIONAL AND FAIL OPEN -- a goal that cannot be scored is not a goal that fails. NO NEW GATES: this wires a MEASUREMENT into the goal process, refuses nothing about anyone's code, and a project that declines to score must run epics exactly as before.
ticket.title: Wire the scorecard into the epic goal process, for any project
